medications.name: Acetaminophen (Tylenol)

dosage.adults: 325–650 mg every 4–6 hours as needed. Max 3,000 mg/day.
dosage.children: 10–15 mg/kg every 4–6 hours. Do not exceed 5 doses in 24 hours.

side_effects: Liver damage with overdose or alcohol use
warnings: Do not exceed recommended dose
Avoid alcohol while taking this medication
Check other medications for hidden acetaminophen (e.g. cold remedies)

medications.name: Ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin)

dosage.adults: 200–400 mg every 4–6 hours. Max 1,200 mg/day (OTC). Up to 3,200 mg/day under medical supervision.
dosage.children: 5–10 mg/kg every 6–8 hours. Not for infants under 6 months.

warnings: Take with food to reduce stomach upset
Avoid if you have kidney disease, ulcers, or are on blood thinners
Avoid in last trimester of pregnancy
Can increase risk of heart attack and stroke with long-term use

medications.name: Loratadine (Claritin)

dosage.children: Children 6+: 10 mg once daily. Children 2–5: 5 mg once daily.

warnings: Non-drowsy but may still cause drowsiness in some people
Use caution when driving until you know how it affects you
Consult doctor if you have liver or kidney disease

medications.name: Diphenhydramine (Benadryl)

dosage.children: Children 6–11: 12.5–25 mg every 4–6 hours. Not recommended under 6 without doctor's advice.

warnings: Causes significant drowsiness — do not drive or operate machinery
Avoid alcohol
Avoid in elderly patients (risk of falls, confusion)
Do not use as a long-term sleep aid

medications.name: Ondansetron (Zofran)

dosage.adults: 4–8 mg every 8 hours as needed. Prescription only.
dosage.children: Dose varies by weight and age. Always follow physician instructions.

warnings: Prescription only — do not use without medical supervision
Can affect heart rhythm (QT prolongation) — inform doctor of heart conditions
Not recommended in first trimester of pregnancy without physician approval

medications.name: Amoxicillin

dosage.adults: 250–500 mg every 8 hours, or 500–875 mg every 12 hours, for 7–10 days. Prescription only.
dosage.children: 25–45 mg/kg/day divided every 8–12 hours. Always follow physician instructions.

warnings: Prescription only
Inform doctor of penicillin allergy
Complete the full course even if feeling better
Can reduce effectiveness of oral contraceptives

medications.name: Sumatriptan (Imitrex)

dosage.adults: 25–100 mg at onset. May repeat once after 2 hours. Max 200 mg/day. Prescription only.
dosage.children: Not recommended under 18 without specialist guidance.

warnings: Prescription only
Do not use if you have heart disease, uncontrolled hypertension, or history of stroke
Do not combine with MAO inhibitors or other triptans within 24 hours
Most effective when taken at first sign of migraine

medications.name: Oral Rehydration Salts (Pedialyte / Gastrolyte)

dosage.adults: Drink as directed on package. Generally 200–400 mL after each loose stool.
dosage.children: 5–10 mL/kg after each loose stool. Consult package or doctor.

warnings: Not a replacement for medical care in severe dehydration
Seek medical help if unable to keep fluids down
Do not give plain water to infants in place of ORS

medications.name: Metformin

dosage.adults: 500 mg twice daily or 850 mg once daily with meals. Titrated up slowly. Prescription only.
dosage.children: 10 years and older: 500 mg twice daily. Always follow physician instructions.

warnings: Prescription only
Hold before contrast dye procedures (CT scan)
Avoid excess alcohol
Not for use in severe kidney or liver disease

medications.name: Lorazepam (Ativan)

dosage.adults: 0.5–2 mg 2–3 times daily as needed. Prescription only.
dosage.children: Not typically recommended for children for anxiety. Always follow physician instructions.

warnings: Prescription only — controlled substance
High risk of dependence and withdrawal
Do not stop suddenly without physician guidance
Avoid alcohol and other CNS depressants
Do not drive or operate machinery
